vn-final-anatomy-01-02-1.text: Vertebrae and ribs develop from the {{c1::sclerotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-2.text: The nucleus pulposus is a remnant of the {{c1::notochord}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-3.text: The annulus fibrosus develops from the {{c1::sclerotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-4.text: The epaxial muscles are supplied by the {{c1::dorsal primary rami}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-5.text: The hypaxial muscles are supplied by the {{c1::ventral primary rami}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-6.text: The primary ossification center of a long bone forms in the {{c1::diaphysis}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-7.text: Secondary ossification centers of long bones form in the {{c1::epiphyses}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-8.text: The lateral plate mesoderm supplies the limb bones and cartilage; limb muscle precursors come from the {{c1::myotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-9.text: The upper limb rotates laterally during development; the lower limb rotates {{c1::medially}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-10.text: Premature closure of the sagittal suture causes {{c1::scaphocephaly}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-1.text: The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and {{c1::tensor fasciae latae}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-2.text: Gluteus maximus is supplied by the {{c1::inferior gluteal nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-3.text: On a Trendelenburg test, the pelvis drops on the side {{c1::opposite the affected stance leg}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-4.text: Piriformis divides the greater sciatic foramen into spaces above and below it; the superior gluteal nerve exits {{c1::above piriformis}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-5.text: The main nerve of the medial thigh compartment is the {{c1::obturator nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-6.text: The anterior cruciate ligament limits anterior translation of the {{c1::tibia relative to the femur}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-7.text: The posterior cruciate ligament limits posterior translation of the {{c1::tibia relative to the femur}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-8.text: The medial meniscus is attached to the {{c1::tibial collateral ligament}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-9.text: The muscle that unlocks the extended knee is the {{c1::popliteus}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-10.text: The patellar ligament attaches to the {{c1::tibial tuberosity}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-1.text: The lumbar plexus forms mainly from the anterior rami of {{c1::L1–L4}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-2.text: The femoral nerve emerges from the lateral border of {{c1::psoas major}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-3.text: The obturator nerve emerges from the medial border of {{c1::psoas major}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-4.text: The femoral and obturator nerves both receive fibers from {{c1::L2–L4}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-5.text: The saphenous nerve is a sensory branch of the {{c1::femoral nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-6.text: From lateral to medial, the major structures in the femoral triangle are {{c1::nerve, artery, vein and femoral canal}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-7.text: The major structure outside the femoral sheath is the {{c1::femoral nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-8.text: The medial compartment of the femoral sheath is the {{c1::femoral canal}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-9.text: The femoral artery becomes the popliteal artery after passing through the {{c1::adductor hiatus}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-10.text: The deepest major neurovascular structure in the popliteal fossa is the {{c1::popliteal artery}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-1.text: Koplik spots in a child with cough, coryza and conjunctivitis point to {{c1::measles}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-2.text: Cataracts, deafness and congenital heart defects are characteristic of {{c1::congenital rubella syndrome}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-3.text: Parvovirus B19 can cause transient aplastic crisis because it infects {{c1::erythroid precursors}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-4.text: In roseola, the rash typically appears after the {{c1::fever subsides}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-5.text: Chickenpox can show macules, papules, vesicles and crusts {{c1::at the same time}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-6.text: A common long-term complication of shingles is {{c1::postherpetic neuralgia}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-7.text: Human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 commonly cause {{c1::anogenital warts}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-8.text: Human papillomavirus types 16 and 18 are associated with {{c1::cervical cancer}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-9.text: Molluscum contagiosum typically causes dome-shaped papules with {{c1::central umbilication}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-10.text: Hand, foot and mouth disease can be caused by Coxsackie A viruses of the genus {{c1::Enterovirus}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-1.text: A first-line option for predominantly comedonal acne is a topical {{c1::retinoid}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-2.text: Benzoyl peroxide kills Cutibacterium acnes by releasing {{c1::free oxygen radicals}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-3.text: Topical clindamycin is paired with benzoyl peroxide to limit {{c1::antibiotic resistance}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-4.text: Common local adverse effects of topical retinoids include {{c1::dryness, peeling and irritation}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-5.text: An acne agent that can also reduce hyperpigmentation is {{c1::azelaic acid}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-6.text: Oral isotretinoin is used for severe nodulocystic acne and is strongly {{c1::teratogenic}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-7.text: Two laboratory abnormalities associated with isotretinoin are {{c1::raised liver enzymes and triglycerides}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-8.text: Estrogen in combined oral contraceptives lowers free testosterone in part by increasing {{c1::sex hormone-binding globulin}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-9.text: Spironolactone helps hormonal acne in part by blocking {{c1::androgen receptors}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-10.text: An example of topical therapy for papulopustular rosacea is {{c1::metronidazole}}.
